Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Date of Admission: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Hospital Course:
The patient, a 69-year-old male with a known duodenal diverticulum and remote history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery, was admitted to the hospital with bilateral upper quadrant abdominal pain for several weeks, nausea, abdominal distension, and food intolerance. A CT scan revealed a distended gastric remnant and a possible bowel obstruction.

The patient was taken to the operating room for an exploratory laparotomy where a 4.5 cm enterolith was found and removed from the distal jejunum. A cholecystectomy was also performed during which gallstones were discovered. The patient had an uneventful recovery and was discharged on postoperative day 8.

Follow-up:
At the patient's postoperative visit, two weeks after surgery, he was reported to be in good health. Unfortunately, the patient was lost to follow-up after one month.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Summary:
This 69-year-old male presented with bilateral upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, abdominal distension, and food intolerance. He was found to have a distended gastric remnant and a bowel obstruction caused by a 4.5 cm enterolith containing bile salts. Treatment included an exploratory laparotomy and enterolith removal, as well as a cholecystectomy. The patient had an uneventful recovery and was discharged on postoperative day 8. It is unfortunate that the patient was lost to follow-up after one month.

text:
**Principal diagnosis: K56.4 Other obstruction of intestine** (enterolith/gallstone-type intraluminal obstruction)

**Rationale**
- The condition occasioning the admission and treated by laparotomy was a small bowel obstruction caused by a 4.5 cm enterolith in the distal jejunum.
- In ICD-10-AM, K56.4 "Other obstruction of intestine" includes obstruction by enterolith and is the usual code for intraluminal obstruction by a foreign body or concretion. K56.3 (gallstone ileus) applies only if the stone is a gallstone that has passed through a biliary-enteric fistula. Here the enterolith contained bile salts, but no fistula or gallstone origin is documented, so K56.4 is the better fit.
- Note that K56.4 is in the K56 block, which in ICD-10-AM 8th/9th/10th/11th editions is used with a 5th character only if the edition's tabular list specifies one. Check your edition.

**Secondary diagnoses to consider**
- K80.20 Calculus of gallbladder without cholecystitis (gallstones found incidentally, cholecystectomy performed)
- K57.10 Diverticulum of small intestine without perforation, abscess, or bleeding (duodenal diverticulum)
- Z98.0 Intestinal bypass and anastomosis status (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass)
- K31.0 Acute dilatation of stomach, if the distended gastric remnant is documented by the clinician as a diagnosis

**Procedures (ACHI)**
- Laparotomy with enterotomy and removal of the enterolith
- Cholecystectomy

Final code assignment should follow the full record and your local coding standards.
